subject: nutrition-dietetics
intro: Nutrition and dietetics turns the science of food into care, leading to work counselling patients, running food-service programmes, improving community health and teaching the science of eating well.

roles.title: Dietitians and Nutritionists
roles.what: Plan and conduct food-service or nutritional programmes that promote health and control disease, supervise food-service departments, counsel individuals and conduct nutritional research.
roles.where: The nutrition-care process and counselling topics of unit 8, the clinical-nutrition units on chronic and acute care, and the nutritional-assessment unit are the working method of the profession.

roles.title: Community Health Workers
roles.what: Promote health within communities, helping people adopt healthy behaviours, advocating for their health needs and implementing programmes that improve individual and overall community health.
roles.where: The public-health nutrition unit — food environments and policy, programme planning and evaluation, health equity and food security — is the community-programme toolkit this role uses daily.

roles.title: Family and Consumer Sciences Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach courses in childcare, family relations, finance, nutrition and related subjects pertaining to home management, combining teaching with research in those fields.
roles.where: Life-span nutrition — pregnancy, childhood, ageing — plus the digestion-and-metabolism units and the evidence-based-practice strand are the core of the nutrition courses these teachers deliver.
